Justice Catherine Bachi-Mzawazi, sitting in Chinhoyi, dismissed Florence Muoni's bid for sole custody of her three minor children, ruling that there was no justification to uproot them from their existing environment with their father and stepmother. The court instead granted Muoni access to the children during the first two weeks of every school holiday and directed their father, Joseph Dzotizeyi, to consult her on guardianship matters as and when the need arises. Tagwirei, who was appointed Minister of Economic Development in Mnangagwa's Cabinet a week ago, is being tipped to take over from him. A statement, signed by party spokesperson Christopher Mutsvangwa, confirmed his appointment and the relegation of once powerful general secretary Obert Mpofu, who has now been demoted to Zanu PF's Council of Elders. "Comrade Emmerson Dambudzo Mnangagwa, through the Secretary General, Cde Jacob Mudenda and in accordance with the Constitution of the Party, specifically Article 7, on the appointment of Central Committee members, Article 8, regarding appointments to the Council of Elders and Article 9, regarding the appointment of Politburo members, has made the following appointments and redeployments. Xi presented the principles during a meeting with Togo's President of the Council of Ministers, Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, who was on an official visit to China on October 13, according to China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The remarks come as several African regions continue to face conflict and security challenges, including Sudan, the Great Lakes region and the Horn of Africa, where regional and international efforts have sought to advance ceasefires, dialogue and lasting political settlements. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn Xi said African people should remain central to decisions affecting the continent, insisting that outside parties involved in resolving conflicts should respect Africa's leadership in regional affairs. "African people are the true masters of the continent and should therefore play a central role in regional affairs," Xi said, according to the Chinese Foreign Ministry. His first principle emphasised African leadership, positioning the continent's people and regional actors at the centre of efforts to resolve conflicts.

More than 4,000 people have died in five months, but the response is beginning to show results, as teams work to rebuild confidence in health services, protect women and children and support survivors. This was one of the first major atrocities during what became known as the First Congo War, helping to unleash decades of foreign-backed rebellions and grave abuses against civilians by all sides, including ethnic-based massacres , widespread rape and sexual violence , forced recruitment of children, abductions , torture, mutilation , and forced displacement . The Congolese Nobel Peace Prize laureate, Dr. Denis Mukwege, began his career as a doctor at Lemera hospital, and he was there on October 6, 1996 when the place he thought was safe, protected by international humanitarian law, became the scene of carnage. Mukwege has since dedicated his life to supporting survivors of sexual violence in the Democratic Republic of Congo and to advocating justice for victims.

Situated in the Horn of Africa and bordering Sudan, Ethiopia and Djibouti, it became a sovereign state after gaining independence from Ethiopia in 1993 following a 30-year war. The unilateral electoral process adopted by former President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, whose term in office expired in May this year, poses a serious threat to Somalia's statehood and future. It risks paving the way for competing electoral processes and the outbreak of civil conflict across the country. Given that the country's political destiny and the future of its statehood cannot be determined through unilateral decisions or personal ambitions, we call for the continuation of the ongoing dialogue and the urgent holding of inclusive elections. The outgoing President's plan to hold elections without a political consensus, and without the participation or agreement of the Federal Member States and the country's political opposition, reflects his misguided authoritarian approach and disregard for the constitution.

Protests over water shortages and the high cost of living that started a week ago erupted into violence on Friday when a woman was shot and wounded by police at a roadblock. The circumstances of the shooting are not clear, but the officer has since been arrested and remanded in custody. Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam ordered the curfew on Tuesday, warning against those "acting against the interests of the country", which is a tourism and financial services hub. stories.title: Kenya: WHO Urges Vigilance After Kenya Confirms Second Ebola Case
stories.summary: Kenya: WHO Urges Vigilance After Kenya Confirms Second Ebola Case Ardo Farah/WHO A healthcare worker in Kenya prepares Ebola response materials as part of a training exercise. 15 October 2026 UN News Service The World Health Organization (WHO) continues to support Kenya's efforts to contain Ebola after a second person tested positive for the Bundibugyo virus, the UN agency's representative in the country said on Thursday. The patient, a 39-year-old man, is a relative of Kenya's first case - related to the ongoing deadly outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) - who died in hospital on 5 October. He was among contacts who were placed in quarantine and developed symptoms on 13 October. 'We all have a role to play' Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines " I congratulate the Government for taking this important step to ensure that contacts are listed and quarantined ," WHO Representative Dr. Neema Rusibamayila Kimambo told UN News in Nairobi, a day after the Ministry of Health confirmed the new case. "But to defeat this disease, it's not about the Government, it is not about partners It is about everybody," she insisted. " We all have a role to play and if each one of us plays our part, then we should be able to contain the disease and stop community spread ." Casting a wide net Kenya's first Ebola patient and fatality was a local man who had been living in the DRC, where the record outbreak continues to spread in the east. He arrived in Nairobi via Uganda on 3 October and died in hospital two days later.

Ali is the British-Somali boxer who escaped to the UK from the Somali civil war with her family as a refugee, and in 2021 became the first person to box for Somalia at Olympic Games . The boxing significance of her last name is actually not mentioned in the film – and I never noticed it until it flashed up in a kind of “fight card” intertitle before her first competitive bout. She is fiercely played by Jasmine Jobson, from TV’s Top Boy; her supportive white Muslim-convert husband Richard – a hugely important figure in enabling Ramla to break away from her disapproving family and do as she wants – is played by Finn Cole, and her abusive trainer Clinton is Gershwyn Eustache Jr. This is a film that takes you through the classic boxing-movie scenes fluently enough: the nervous first appearance in the gym, the overbearing quasi-parental coach, the heartstopping fight debut.

stories.title: ICJ judge Navi Pillay wins Nobel peace prize for promoting international law
stories.summary: 1:11 Nobel peace prize winner Navi Pillay jokes about sharing award with Donald Trump – video ICJ judge Navi Pillay wins Nobel peace prize for promoting international law Committee recognises work of South African who chaired UN commission that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza The Nobel peace prize has been awarded to Navi Pillay, the South African former UN human rights chief who chaired the UN commission that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza . The Norwegian Nobel committee said Pillay, who is serving as a judge at the international court of justice (ICJ), has “shown that legal measures can help prevent acts of war and violence”. “Navi Pillay’s commitment to universal legal principles and her firm moral compass are constants in a long career,” the committee said, mentioning her early work defending Nelson Mandela under South Africa’s apartheid regime, serving on the international criminal tribunal, and then as the UN high commissioner for human rights, as well as chairing the UN independent international commission of inquiry on the occupied Palestinian territory. That commission concluded last year that the state of Israel was guilty of genocidal acts in Gaza “with the specific intent to destroy Palestinians in Gaza”, and said the country’s prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, its president, Isaac Herzog, and its former defence minister Yoav Gallant had “incited the commission of genocide”. “It is clear that there is an intent to destroy the Palestinians in Gaza through acts that meet the criteria set forth in the genocide convention,” Pillay said on the publication of the commission’s findings in September last year. Israel refused to cooperate with the commission, arguing it was biased, and rejected its report as “scandalous”. The Israeli foreign ministry reacted furiously to news of Pillay’s award on Friday. “If there were an award for lies, hatred, and blood libels, Navi Pillay wouldn’t just be a contender.
